input.quote: 20. INDEMNIFICATION 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.
input.rationale: Section 20 contains only a one-way, unlimited Customer indemnity ("every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services") and no Vendor indemnity at all — neither the preferred position (Vendor IP/breach-of-law/data-breach/wilful-misconduct indemnity with narrow Customer indemnity) nor the fallback (Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies) is met; this is squarely the walk-away case. Section 9.3 also cross-references remedies "required by Section 20.5" that do not exist. The redline inserts the Vendor indemnity, customary exclusions, a standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, and infringement remedies (restoring the 20.5 cross-reference), and narrows Customer's indemnity to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

proposal.summary: Add Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity with standard procedure and infringement remedies; narrow Customer's indemnity
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 20 currently contains only an unlimited Customer indemnity and no Vendor indemnity, which is our walk-away position; we have added a Vendor indemnity for IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused data breach and wilful misconduct, with customary exclusions, defence procedure and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies. We also narrowed Customer's indemnity to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law, and the new Section 20.5 supplies the remedies Section 9.3 already cross-references.

ops.oldText: 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.
ops.newText: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

ops.text: 20.2 Section 20.1(a) does not apply to the extent a claim arises from Customer's unauthorized modification of the Services or Deliverables, their combination with items not supplied or recommended by Vendor where the claim would have been avoided absent the combination, or Vendor's compliance with Customer's written specifications.

20.3 The indemnified Party shall give prompt written notice of the claim, permit the indemnifying Party to control the defence and settlement (provided that no settlement imposing liability or an admission on the indemnified Party is made without its prior written consent), and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense. The indemnified Party may participate with its own counsel at its own cost.

20.4 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from and against third-party claims to the extent arising out of Customer Data or other content Customer provides to the Services in breach of this Agreement, or Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

20.5 If the Services or Deliverables are, or in Vendor's reasonable opinion may become, the subject of a claim under Section 20.1(a), Vendor shall at its own expense procure for Customer the right to continue using the affected item, or modify or replace it with a functionally equivalent non-infringing item. If neither remedy is reasonably available, Customer may terminate the affected Services or Deliverables and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees and Fees paid for the affected Deliverables.
